_comment: Current bills, full lens (v391). The anchor is H.R. 8352 (119th), the Criminal History Access Act of 2026, which passed both chambers (Senate by unanimous consent on 2026-09-30) and awaits presentment. The sweep is every public law signed in October 2026 — GovInfo's BILLSTATUS records show exactly six: H.R. 5345 (119-119), S. 766 (119-120), S. 195 (119-121), S. 240 (119-122), S. 283 (119-123) and S. 2403 (119-124) — and the Utah 2026 General Session data-center bills with enrolled text: H.B. 76 and H.B. 507, both signed. Every 2026GS House and Senate bill record on le.utah.gov was read for data centers and large loads; the three others found (`notEnrolled`) were filed and never passed. Each measure is created in netlify/database/migrations/20261118000000_vr_current_bills_full_lens.sql with every issue its enrolled text touches as a vr_measure_issues row (no primary gate: secondary rows carry their own weight; exactly one row per measure is flagged primary for surfacing). A mapping is pinned by verbatim `sources` quotes from the enrolled text (and, for S. 240's Yellowtail row, the base law it amends) and by `touches`, each a phrase in those quotes tied to a word of the issue's own label, chip or keywords. An effect line is written only where the text makes a concrete insert, strike or new requirement on that issue; a mapped pair whose only change another line on the same act already states is `silent` with `why`. A measure no issue fits has `noMappingWhy` and no rows. `considered` lists issues read and declined. No roll call, member vote or presidential or gubernatorial position is added, so no member's file, score or Direction Match moves; S. 2403's House roll 119/2/314 is noted, not seeded. Lines are stored once in consistency.js _DOS_EFFECT under the CURRENT BILLS SLICE 20 marker.

measures.title: Criminal History Access Act of 2026
measures.statusPer: Passed the House; passed the Senate without amendment by Unanimous Consent on 2026-09-30; message on Senate action sent to the House on 2026-10-14; not yet presented to the President (GovInfo BILLSTATUS).
measures.summary: Amends 28 U.S.C. 534 so the Attorney General exchanges criminal history records with state peace officer standards and training agencies — state agencies that set standards for hiring, training, ethical conduct and retention of law enforcement officers — and directs the Attorney General to amend 28 CFR part 20 within 180 days. Passed both chambers (Senate by unanimous consent on 2026-09-30); awaiting presentment.
measures.tense: Passed both chambers and is not yet law, so its line opens “Would”.

mappings.rationale: The act adds state peace officer standards and training agencies — agencies with authority "to set standards for the hiring, training, ethical conduct, and retention of the law enforcement officers of the State" — to those the FBI exchanges criminal history records with, so the agencies that certify officers can check the records behind those standards. Training and accountability for officers is this key's own pairing.
mappings.line: Would let state agencies that set police hiring, training and ethical conduct standards receive FBI criminal history records.

plain.receive: exchange such records and information with

sources.quote: To authorize peace officer standards and training agencies to access criminal history records, and for other purposes.
SEC. 2. FEDERAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION.

exchange such records and information with, and for the official use of, authorized officials of the Federal Government, including the United States Sentencing Commission, the States, including State sentencing commissions and peace officer standards and training agencies, Indian tribes, cities, and penal and other institutions

the term `peace officer standards and training agency' means an agency of a State with the statutory authority under State law to set standards for the hiring, training, ethical conduct, and retention of the law enforcement officers of the State through certification, licensing, or other similar qualification process

mappings.rationale: The same clause widens the set of agencies the federal government transfers criminal history records to — a government's transfer of records about a person, which is inside this key's scope — so a yea widens that sharing rather than narrowing it.
mappings.why: The act’s one change on this issue is the same widened exchange the justice_balance line states; a second line would restate it.

sources.quote: exchange such records and information with, and for the official use of, authorized officials of the Federal Government, including the United States Sentencing Commission, the States, including State sentencing commissions and peace officer standards and training agencies, Indian tribes, cities, and penal and other institutions

measures.title: Crow Tribe Water Rights Settlement Amendments Act of 2025
measures.statusPer: Signed by the President and became Public Law 119-122 on 2026-10-15 (GovInfo BILLSTATUS).
measures.summary: Amends the Crow Tribe Water Rights Settlement Act of 2010: repeals the MR&I System section, creates an MR&I Projects Account the Tribe must use first for water production, treatment or delivery infrastructure, keeps title to those projects in the Tribe with no federal operation and maintenance obligation, and extends from 15 to 20 years the deadline in section 412(b)(1) for the Tribe’s exclusive right to develop power at Yellowtail Afterbay Dam. Public Law 119-122, signed 2026-10-15.
measures.tense: Public Law 119-122, so its lines read as done.

mappings.rationale: The new MR&I Projects Account must be used first "to plan, permit, design, engineer, construct, reconstruct, replace, rehabilitate, operate, or repair water production, treatment, or delivery infrastructure" — building the supply side of water, which is this key.
mappings.line: Created an MR&I Projects Account the Crow Tribe must use first for water production, treatment or delivery infrastructure.

plain.must use first: Priority use of funds.--The Tribe shall use funds

sources.quote: MR&I Projects Account, to be established as soon as practicable after the date of enactment of the Crow Tribe Water Rights Settlement Amendments Act of 2025

Priority use of funds.--The Tribe shall use funds from the MR&I Projects Account-- ``(I) to plan, permit, design, engineer, construct, reconstruct, replace, rehabilitate, operate, or repair water production, treatment, or delivery infrastructure, including for domestic and municipal use or wastewater infrastructure

mappings.rationale: The same account funds water production, treatment, delivery and wastewater infrastructure, which this key names as "water systems".
mappings.why: The act’s one change on this issue is the MR&I Projects Account the water_storage line states; a second line would restate it.

sources.quote: Priority use of funds.--The Tribe shall use funds from the MR&I Projects Account-- ``(I) to plan, permit, design, engineer, construct, reconstruct, replace, rehabilitate, operate, or repair water production, treatment, or delivery infrastructure, including for domestic and municipal use or wastewater infrastructure

mappings.rationale: Section 412(b)(1) gives the Tribe "the exclusive right to develop and market power generation on the Yellowtail Afterbay Dam", lost if construction is not substantially complete within the period; the act lengthens that period from 15 to 20 years, keeping a hydropower project open.
mappings.line: Extended the Crow Tribe’s exclusive right to develop power at Yellowtail Afterbay Dam from 15 to 20 years absent substantial construction.

plain.absent: if construction has not been substantially completed

sources.quote: Subsection (b)(1) of section 412 of the Crow Tribe Water Rights Settlement Act of 2010 (Public Law 111-291; 124 Stat. 3116) is amended by striking ``15 years'' and inserting ``20 years''.

the Tribe shall have the exclusive right to develop and market power generation on the Yellowtail Afterbay Dam, provided that this exclusive right shall expire 15 years after the date of enactment of this Act if construction has not been substantially completed on the power generation project of the Tribe.

measures.title: Billion Dollar Boondoggle Act of 2025
measures.statusPer: Signed by the President and became Public Law 119-120 on 2026-10-07 (GovInfo BILLSTATUS).
measures.summary: Requires the OMB Director to issue guidance under which executive and independent regulatory agencies report each year on every project more than 5 years behind schedule or at least $1 billion over its original cost estimate (projects funded through direct spending excluded), and to submit and post an annual report. Public Law 119-120, signed 2026-10-07.
measures.tense: Public Law 119-120, so its line reads as done.

mappings.rationale: The act requires an annual public report of "taxpayer-funded projects that are over budget and behind schedule" — cost overruns and delays named project by project, with the explanation for each — which is the waste-and-accountability work this key describes.
mappings.line: Required OMB to report yearly on projects not funded by direct spending that are over 5 years late or $1 billion or more over cost estimate.

sources.quote: To require an annual report of taxpayer-funded projects that are over budget and behind schedule.

(A) that is more than 5 years behind schedule, as measured against the original expected date for completion; or (B) for which the amount spent on the project is not less than $1,000,000,000 more than the original cost estimate for the project;
that is not funded through direct spending

(2) Report.--The Director shall submit to Congress and post on the website of the Office of Management and Budget an annual report containing the information submitted under paragraph (1) for the relevant year.

mappings.rationale: Each covered agency must submit, every year, the original and current cost estimate, the federal share, each contractor and grant recipient, and the amount of and rationale for any award or bonus on the project — an audit of agency spending by project.
mappings.why: The act’s one change on this issue is the annual project report the gov_waste line states; a second line would restate it.

sources.quote: submit to the Director information relating to each covered project of the covered agency

measures.title: Improving Social Security’s Service to Victims of Identity Theft Act
measures.statusPer: Signed by the President and became Public Law 119-119 on 2026-10-07 (GovInfo BILLSTATUS).
measures.summary: Adds section 714 to the Social Security Act: the Commissioner must give any individual whose Social Security number has been misused, or whose card was lost in transmission, a single point of contact — a team of specially trained employees accountable for the case until it is resolved. Takes effect 180 days after enactment. Public Law 119-119, signed 2026-10-07.
measures.tense: Public Law 119-119, so its line reads as done.

mappings.rationale: The act changes how the Social Security Administration handles beneficiaries and card holders whose numbers were misused, including "to fraudulently obtain benefits": one accountable contact until the case is resolved. It protects the program's beneficiaries and their records, which is this key.
mappings.line: Required Social Security to give anyone whose Social Security number was misused a single point of contact until the case is resolved.

plain.resolved: throughout the resolution of the individual's case
plain.give: shall establish and implement procedures to ensure

sources.quote: The Commissioner of Social Security shall establish and implement procedures to ensure that any individual whose social security account number has been misused (such as to fraudulently obtain benefits under title II, VIII, or XVI of this Act
has a single point of contact at the Social Security Administration throughout the resolution of the individual's case.

mappings.rationale: The single point of contact is a public service the Social Security Administration must now provide to identity-theft victims.
mappings.why: The act’s one change on this issue is the single point of contact the social_security line states; a second line would restate it.

sources.quote: has a single point of contact at the Social Security Administration throughout the resolution of the individual's case.

measures.title: Illegal Red Snapper and Tuna Enforcement Act
measures.statusPer: Signed by the President and became Public Law 119-123 on 2026-10-15 (GovInfo BILLSTATUS).
measures.summary: Directs NIST and NOAA, consulting CBP and the Coast Guard, to develop a chemical-analysis method and portable field kit for identifying the country of origin of seafood to support enforcement against illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing and seafood fraud, with pilot studies on red snapper and tuna and a report within 2 years. Public Law 119-123, signed 2026-10-15.
measures.noMappingWhy: No issue in the vocabulary covers fisheries enforcement or seafood fraud. The trade keys are about tariffs, manufacturing and China, and the text names neither imports nor domestic industry; the environment keys are about air, water, land and energy. Mapping it would invent an issue the text does not touch.

measures.title: American Music Tourism Act of 2025
measures.statusPer: Signed by the President and became Public Law 119-121 on 2026-10-09 (GovInfo BILLSTATUS).
measures.summary: Adds music tourism to the Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Travel and Tourism’s duties to promote domestic and international travel, rewrites the international travel facilitation subsection, defines music tourism, and adds a biennial report. Public Law 119-121, signed 2026-10-09.
measures.noMappingWhy: No issue in the vocabulary covers tourism promotion. The act directs an office to identify and promote destinations and report; it changes no tax, regulation, wage, trade or spending rule that an economic key reads.

measures.title: Retire through Ownership Act
measures.statusPer: Signed by the President and became Public Law 119-124 on 2026-10-15 (GovInfo BILLSTATUS); the House roll call is 119/2/314 on 2026-09-16.
measures.summary: Amends ERISA section 3(18) so a fiduciary of an employee ownership plan may rely in good faith on an independent appraiser’s valuation that follows IRS Revenue Ruling 59-60 when determining the fair market value of closely held shares, without expanding the Labor Secretary’s authority or modifying fiduciary duties under section 404. Public Law 119-124, signed 2026-10-15.
measures.noMappingWhy: The keys that come near — Raise Wages & Protect Workers, Balanced Prosperity, Protect Social Security — state no side on how a retirement-plan fiduciary values closely held shares. The text adds a good-faith reliance rule while expressly leaving fiduciary obligations under section 404 unchanged, so no direction on any of them can be read from it without inventing one.

measures.title: Data Center Water Transparency Amendments
measures.statusPer: Governor Signed 3/23/2026 (le.utah.gov action history); effective May 6, 2026.
measures.summary: This bill addresses reporting related to water use and large data centers.

mappings.rationale: Enacted 73-5-8.3 makes the operator of a new large data center (annual water withdrawal of 75 acre feet or more) report its estimated withdrawals before construction and its actual withdrawals every year, and the Division of Water Rights must publish each center's withdrawal data, "and not in the aggregate", with a fine of up to $100 a day for a missing report. Requiring data centers to account for the water they draw is this key's protective position.
mappings.line: Required operators of new large data centers to report water withdrawals before construction and yearly, and the state to publish them.

plain.operators: the operator of the large data center
plain.construction: before the operator of a large data center begins construction activities

sources.quote: [+(d)"Large data center" means a facility with an annual water withdrawal of 75 acre feet per year or more that:(i)houses a group of networked server computers in one physical location to disseminate, manage, and store data and information as the primary service of the facility;+]
[+(f)"New large data center" means a large data center that begins operations on or after July 1, 2026.+]
[+(b)report to the division:(i)the municipality, if applicable, and county in which the new large data center will be located;+]
[+(ii)the estimated withdrawal amount of water that the new large data center will withdraw annually;+]

[+(4)(a)Subject to Subsection (4)(b), after a new large data center begins operation, the operator of the large data center shall report to the division for the calendar year being reported on:(i)efforts made to reduce water consumption over the calendar year;+]
[+(ii)actual withdrawals for the calendar year;+]

[+(5)(a)The division shall publish water withdrawal data for each new large data center that is reported under Subsection (3)(b) or (4)(a) on the division's public website by no later than September 1 for the previous calendar year, and not in the aggregate.+]
[+(b)"Division" means the Division of Water Rights.+]

[+(3)On or after July 1, 2026, at least 90 days, but no sooner than 360 days, before the operator of a large data center begins construction activities related to a new large data center, the operator of the large data center shall:

mappings.rationale: Before construction, the operator must tell the water provider the new center's "anticipated water consumption needs" so the provider can judge whether that consumption "is compatible with the location" — measuring water demand at the point of siting, which is inside this key's demand-side scope.
mappings.line: Made each new data center using 75 acre feet a year or more notify its water provider of anticipated consumption before building.

sources.quote: [+(3)On or after July 1, 2026, at least 90 days, but no sooner than 360 days, before the operator of a large data center begins construction activities related to a new large data center, the operator of the large data center shall:(a)notify in writing the water provider that provides water to the area where the new large data center will be located to detail the anticipated water consumption needs of the new large data center so that the water provider can determine whether the anticipated water consumption of the new large data center is compatible with the location in which the new large data center is being located; and+]

[+(d)"Large data center" means a facility with an annual water withdrawal of 75 acre feet per year or more that:(i)houses a group of networked server computers in one physical location to disseminate, manage, and store data and information as the primary service of the facility;+]
[+(f)"New large data center" means a large data center that begins operations on or after July 1, 2026.+]

considered.why: The act changes no incentive, siting permission or tax treatment for data centers; it adds reporting duties only.
The act is about water withdrawal and discharge; it says nothing about power demand or utility costs.

measures.summary: This bill addresses local and regional economic development projects and related provisions.

mappings.rationale: The larger operative change creates a new capture district: a county may distribute to the agency "the percentage of property tax increment established by the committee... not to exceed: (A)70%" and the agency "may issue bonds". Counter-provision: after January 1, 2028 the committee "may not approve a proposal for a housing and transit reinvestment zone, a first home investment zone, or a convention center reinvestment zone" unless pending, and new home ownership promotion zones end.
mappings.line: Created regionally significant development zones that capture property tax increment and let their agencies issue bonds.

Counter-provision: incentives remain allowed inside a regionally significant development zone and from up to 80% of county energy excise tax revenue, and pre-May 6, 2027 agreements continue.
mappings.line: Barred local tax-increment incentives to large load data centers starting May 6, 2027, with exceptions.

[+As used in this part:(1)"Incentive" means a payment of public funds, funded by tax increment or personal property tax revenue:(a)from a political subdivision to a person;+]

Counter-provision: a levying county "may provide up to 80% of the revenue generated by the county energy excise tax as an incentive to a large load data center".

The State Reinvestment Restricted Account may also be used for "development of energy resources".

Counter-provision: the new account lists "income tax relief" as a use, subject to appropriation, with no rate change.

considered.why: Rests only on uses the new State Reinvestment Restricted Account “is to be used, subject to appropriation, for”, including water infrastructure and the Great Salt Lake watershed; the bill appropriates nothing to either, so it makes no concrete change on water.

Rests only on the same account’s permitted use for regionally significant transit and on objectives a transit-oriented zone proposal must address; the bill funds no transit, and the zone itself is the development-district row.

Only water link is that an energy-implication zone is approved if land is suitable for a large load data center based on access to electricity and "adequate water supply" (63N-3a-403(1)(a)(ii)); a siting criterion, not a water-use limit, cooling rule or ag-water restriction.

First home investment zone and home ownership promotion zone creation ends after 2027 while a new first home village zone type with owner-occupancy terms is created; per SCOPE (dev_district_finance) these are tightened and loosened in the same text and are secondary to the financing tool.

Density and housing minimums ride inside the new increment zones (63N-3a-301/302) while older housing zones sunset; mixed and secondary to the financing mechanism per SCOPE; no zoning or permitting loosening.
Affordable-unit percentages are conditions of zone proposals, not funding or renter protections; mixed and secondary per SCOPE.
Bill reallocates property tax increment and regulates PIDs (dissolution, closing disclosure) but does not lower or cap what households pay; SCOPE says a PID levy is not property tax relief.
No change to rent, grocery, gas or utility prices; the energy excise tax applies only to high-impact consumers.
The 79-6-1104 exception reaches all non-nuclear projects (fossil and clean alike; intermittent projects were already exempt), so direction on clean energy is indeterminate; no emissions provisions.
Chip is federal business deregulation; per SCOPE, tax-increment districts are targeted subsidy, not rollback. Nothing federal.
Bill allocates authority between the state and local governments, not state versus federal.
No eminent domain or takings change; PID 100% surface-owner consent for creation/annexation is pre-existing law; dissolution asset distribution to owners is incidental.
